preconditions.text: Every freshly deployed proxy starts with the initialized flag at zero.; The initialize function in DistributionCreator (and Distributor) uses only the initializer modifier and has no access control on the caller.; Both contracts are set up behind UUPS proxies where the constructor with initializer runs only on the implementation, not on each proxy instance.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: Because of that, every freshly deployed proxy starts with the initialized flag at zero, and the first external address to call initialize gets to set the accessControlManager (and also the distributor address and default fees in DistributionCreator). If an attacker deploys a malicious accessControlManager that always treats them as governor or guardian, they can initialize the proxy to point to this contract. From that point on, all onlyGovernor, onlyGovernorOrGuardian, and onlyUpgradeableInstance checks are effectively under attacker control, giving them full admin over DistributionCreator and Distributor.

When I checked the initialize function in DistributionCreator, I noticed it only uses the initializer modifier and has no access control on the caller. Distributor follows the same pattern. Both contracts are set up for use behind UUPS proxies, where the constructor with initializer runs only on the implementation, not on each proxy instance.

safety.text: Initialization of a proxy should only be performed by an authorized party, not by the first arbitrary external caller.
